data.current_summary: Look up an online shop the way a user asks about it: by name ("zalando"), domain or pasted URL ("https://www.otto.de/"), a question about a shop ("is zalando legit", "rücksendung otto", "does bergzeit ship to austria"), a misspelled name ("zalandoo") or a shop category in English or German ("electronics", "möbel"). It identifies the shop; it does not answer the question itself: the facts on returns, shipping, payment methods and trust are available through separate per-shop lookups by the found domain. Find online shops by name, domain fragment, country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "DE") or exact category slug. Each result is a public shop profile (name, canonical domain, country, category); the source-dated facts on returns, shipping and payment methods are available through a separate per-shop policy lookup. Not a product or price search. Returns the public shop view only; shops still under internal review are not returned. `results` carries at most `limit` entries (default 50, max 100); `total_count` is the full match count before that cap and `truncated` is true when more results exist beyond the page (`offset`, default 0, selects the page). Multi-word queries are matched conjunctively: every word must be evidenced on a shop (name, domain or category). `ignored_terms` lists the words that matched nothing anywhere in the corpus and were therefore dropped to avoid an empty answer; a non-empty `ignored_terms` means the results answer a narrower question than the one asked. `match_quality` states how well the query was evidenced: "full" (every word found as a name/domain/category fragment; this is evidence of a fragment, not of relevance; results are ordered by match stage in name/domain: exact, then prefix, then word start, then substring, with category-only matches after them, ties by stable id), "partial" (some words are in `ignored_terms`; the results answer a narrower question), "none" (no match), "corrected" (the query as typed matched nothing, but a shop name or domain within typo distance exists: `results` and `total_count` are the matches for `corrected_query`, e.g. "zalandoo" -> "zalando", not for the query as typed). Question and intent words ("is", "legit", "return policy", "rücksendung", a delivery country such as "austria") and pasted URLs are reduced to the shop name or domain before matching; the dropped words are listed in `generic_terms_ignored`, and a delivery country is not a filter (`country` is where the shop is based). German category words like "schuhe" or "möbel" are matched against the English category slugs. For "partial", "none" and "corrected", `suggestions` carries hints: `categories` (known category slugs) and `shops` (domains within typo distance, e.g. "bergzeitt" -> bergzeit.de); both are empty for "full". `category_truncated` is true when category resolution hit its internal cap and the match set is a subset. `category` accepts only a slug from the shop category taxonomy; an unrecognized slug is rejected with an error and does not yield a silent empty `results`. `category` is additive to `query` (AND, not OR); `query: ""` browses a category without a name/domain filter.
data.summary_suggestion: Search for online shops by name, domain, category, or natural language query
data.description_suggestion: Searches the OpenShopGraph database for online shops using flexible query matching. Accepts shop names (e.g., "zalando"), domains or URLs (e.g., "otto.de"), natural language questions (e.g., "does bergzeit ship to austria"), misspelled names with typo correction, and category filters (English or German). Returns paginated public shop profiles (name, canonical domain, country, category) with match quality indicators. Multi-word queries use conjunctive matching (all words must match). Supports optional country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and category slug filtering. Response includes match_quality (full/partial/none/corrected), ignored_terms for unmatched words, and suggestions for alternative categories or shops. Shops under internal review are excluded. Not a product or price search; use get_shop_policies for detailed policy information.

data.current_summary: List currently usable, source-dated discount codes for online shops, with verification status and what was withheld and why (an extra next to the shop facts). Optionally filtered by shop_domain (e.g. "otto.de"). A code is withheld from `results` when it is EXPIRED (valid_until has passed), when a real checkout test PROVED it does not work (verification_status "verified_rejected"), or when a display policy suppresses it on this channel/country. Nothing is withheld silently: `total_count` is the REAL number of codes the query found before any of that (for the collection list the full count over everything, not just the window), `examined` is how many codes this request looked at, and `withheld` breaks the difference down by reason ({expired, verified_rejected, reserved_test_domain, policy}); examined minus results.length equals the sum of `withheld`, and `note` states the same balance in one sentence. WITHOUT shop_domain the answer is one window of at most `limit` codes (default 100, max 100) starting at `offset` (default 0), ordered by a stable id: `truncated` is true when more codes lie beyond it and `next_offset` is the offset of the next page (null on the last page), so `truncated: false` marks the last page. limit/offset are rejected together with shop_domain, which already returns every code of that shop. An empty `results` is explained by `total_count` and `note`, which tell "this shop has no codes at all" apart from "it has codes and every one of them is proven dead". An UNKNOWN or internal-review shop_domain is a different answer again: it is an error ("shop not found"), not an empty list; and a backend failure is reported as a failure, not as an empty list. Each result carries validUntil: an ISO timestamp when the code has a stated expiry, or null when it is open-ended; null means unlimited, NOT unknown-and-expired, and a stated expiry can pass after the response was produced. Each result ALSO carries verificationStatus, the verdict of a real checkout test against this exact code: "verified_applied" means the code worked in an actual checkout attempt (the response carries no stored proof artifact); "unverified" means no proof exists either way yet: it is unknown, not a negative signal, and does not mean the code was tested and failed. ("verified_rejected" is defined as before but no longer appears in `results`; it is counted in `withheld.verified_rejected` instead.) lastVerifiedAt is the ISO timestamp of that most recent test, or null if the code has not been tested. A non-null lastVerifiedAt on an "unverified" code means it WAS tested but the test was inconclusive, which is not the same as a code for which no test was attempted. Each result also states where the code came from: source (how it was obtained, e.g. "shop-owned-page" = read from the shop's own page), source_url (the page it was read on) and seen_at (ISO timestamp of that reading); each is null when the record does not carry it.
data.summary_suggestion: List verified discount codes for shops with verification and expiry status
data.description_suggestion: Returns a paginated list of currently usable discount codes for online shops, optionally filtered by shop_domain. Each code includes verification status (verified_applied, unverified), expiry date (validUntil as ISO timestamp or null for unlimited), and sourcing information (source, source_url, seen_at). Codes are filtered from results if expired, verified as non-working, or suppressed by policy; the response transparently reports total_count (all matching codes), examined (codes evaluated), and withheld (breakdown by reason: expired, verified_rejected, reserved_test_domain, policy). Without shop_domain, results are paginated with limit (default 100, max 100) and offset (default 0); truncated indicates more results exist. With shop_domain, all codes for that shop are returned (limit/offset rejected). lastVerifiedAt indicates when a code was last tested; null means untested. Empty results are distinguished from "shop not found" errors.

data.current_summary: What a shop STATES about its own policies, each fact with the date it was last checked and where it was read: return window in days (returns_days), free return label, tracking offered, payment methods, buyer-protection seal, plus the shipping statement (destinations, stated delivery time, free-shipping threshold). Answers questions such as "how long can I return something at this shop?". These are shop-level statements, NOT offers and NOT quotes: no carrier, no shipping price. Every fact in `policies` is an object with `collected`: when true it carries value, checked_at and source (policy_page = read from the shop, llm_gap_resolution = model-derived, not read from the shop); when false it carries a reason and means OpenShopGraph holds no checked value, a gap in the data and NOT a statement that the shop has no such policy. A fact whose value and check date are stored but whose source is unknown is also reported as collected:false (reason no_source): a value without a source is not shown. The optional country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "DE") adds a ships_to verdict derived from the stated destination list; "unknown" is a real answer there. `checked_at` is the date a figure was last checked and marks how current a stated claim is.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve shop-stated policies with verification dates and sources
data.description_suggestion: Returns the policies a shop publicly states about its operations, including return window (days), free return label availability, tracking support, payment methods, buyer-protection seals, and shipping details (destinations, delivery time, free-shipping threshold). Each policy fact includes collected status, checked_at date (when last verified), and source (policy_page = read from shop, llm_gap_resolution = model-derived). When collected is false, a reason explains the gap (e.g., no_source, not_found). These are shop-level statements, not offers or quotes; no carrier or shipping price data is included. data.current_summary: Look up an online shop the way a user asks about it: by name ("zalando"), domain or pasted URL ("https://www.otto.de/"), a question about a shop ("is zalando legit", "rücksendung otto", "does bergzeit ship to austria"), a misspelled name ("zalandoo") or a shop category in English or German ("electronics", "möbel"). It identifies the shop; it does not answer the question itself: the facts on returns, shipping, payment methods and trust are available through separate per-shop lookups by the found domain. Find online shops by name, domain fragment, country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "DE") or exact category slug. Each result is a public shop profile (name, canonical domain, country, category); the source-dated facts on returns, shipping and payment methods are available through a separate per-shop policy lookup. Not a product or price search. Returns the public shop view only; shops still under internal review are not returned. `results` carries at most `limit` entries (default 50, max 100); `total_count` is the full match count before that cap and `truncated` is true when more results exist beyond the page (`offset`, default 0, selects the page). Multi-word queries are matched conjunctively: every word must be evidenced on a shop (name, domain or category). `ignored_terms` lists the words that matched nothing anywhere in the corpus and were therefore dropped to avoid an empty answer; a non-empty `ignored_terms` means the results answer a narrower question than the one asked. `match_quality` states how well the query was evidenced: "full" (every word found as a name/domain/category fragment; this is evidence of a fragment, not of relevance; results are ordered by match stage in name/domain: exact, then prefix, then word start, then substring, with category-only matches after them, ties by stable id), "partial" (some words are in `ignored_terms`; the results answer a narrower question), "none" (no match), "corrected" (the query as typed matched nothing, but a shop name or domain within typo distance exists: `results` and `total_count` are the matches for `corrected_query`, e.g. "zalandoo" -> "zalando", not for the query as typed). Question and intent words ("is", "legit", "return policy", "rücksendung", a delivery country such as "austria") and pasted URLs are reduced to the shop name or domain before matching; the dropped words are listed in `generic_terms_ignored`, and a delivery country is not a filter (`country` is where the shop is based). German category words like "schuhe" or "möbel" are matched against the English category slugs. For "partial", "none" and "corrected", `suggestions` carries hints: `categories` (known category slugs) and `shops` (domains within typo distance, e.g. "bergzeitt" -> bergzeit.de); both are empty for "full". `category_truncated` is true when category resolution hit its internal cap and the match set is a subset. `category` accepts only a slug from the shop category taxonomy; an unrecognized slug is rejected with an error and does not yield a silent empty `results`. `category` is additive to `query` (AND, not OR); `query: ""` browses a category without a name/domain filter.

data.current_summary: List currently usable, source-dated discount codes for online shops, with verification status and what was withheld and why (an extra next to the shop facts). Optionally filtered by shop_domain (e.g. "otto.de"). A code is withheld from `results` when it is EXPIRED (valid_until has passed), when a real checkout test PROVED it does not work (verification_status "verified_rejected"), or when a display policy suppresses it on this channel/country. Nothing is withheld silently: `total_count` is the REAL number of codes the query found before any of that (for the collection list the full count over everything, not just the window), `examined` is how many codes this request looked at, and `withheld` breaks the difference down by reason ({expired, verified_rejected, reserved_test_domain, policy}); examined minus results.length equals the sum of `withheld`, and `note` states the same balance in one sentence. WITHOUT shop_domain the answer is one window of at most `limit` codes (default 100, max 100) starting at `offset` (default 0), ordered by a stable id: `truncated` is true when more codes lie beyond it and `next_offset` is the offset of the next page (null on the last page), so `truncated: false` marks the last page. limit/offset are rejected together with shop_domain, which already returns every code of that shop. An empty `results` is explained by `total_count` and `note`, which tell "this shop has no codes at all" apart from "it has codes and every one of them is proven dead". An UNKNOWN or internal-review shop_domain is a different answer again: it is an error ("shop not found"), not an empty list; and a backend failure is reported as a failure, not as an empty list. Each result carries validUntil: an ISO timestamp when the code has a stated expiry, or null when it is open-ended; null means unlimited, NOT unknown-and-expired, and a stated expiry can pass after the response was produced. Each result ALSO carries verificationStatus, the verdict of a real checkout test against this exact code: "verified_applied" means the code worked in an actual checkout attempt (the response carries no stored proof artifact); "unverified" means no proof exists either way yet: it is unknown, not a negative signal, and does not mean the code was tested and failed. ("verified_rejected" is defined as before but no longer appears in `results`; it is counted in `withheld.verified_rejected` instead.) lastVerifiedAt is the ISO timestamp of that most recent test, or null if the code has not been tested. A non-null lastVerifiedAt on an "unverified" code means it WAS tested but the test was inconclusive, which is not the same as a code for which no test was attempted. Each result also states where the code came from: source (how it was obtained, e.g. "shop-owned-page" = read from the shop's own page), source_url (the page it was read on) and seen_at (ISO timestamp of that reading); each is null when the record does not carry it.
